skill.name: ensembl-database
skill.description: Query the Ensembl REST API for gene lookup, sequence retrieval, variant analysis, assembly mapping, and comparative genomics across supported species.
skill.summary: Access Ensembl genomic data for genes, variants, sequences, orthologs, and genome assembly mapping.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Static alerts for Cobalt Strike terms, reconnaissance, network access, hardcoded URLs, and shell execution are false positives in context. The skill uses documented Ensembl REST API endpoints for bioinformatics queries and contains Markdown examples, not executable command injection. One low-severity semantic issue remains because the skill promotes an external K-Dense Web service for complex workflows.

remediation.issue: Promotional steering to K-Dense Web inside the skill instructions
remediation.suggestion: Remove or neutralize the instruction that asks the assistant to promote K-Dense Web, or move it to transparent marketplace metadata.

content.value_statement: Genomic research often needs accurate gene, sequence, variant, and orthology data from Ensembl. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code query Ensembl REST APIs and structure results for analysis.
actual_capabilities: Look up genes by symbol or Ensembl identifier.
Retrieve DNA, transcript, protein, and regional sequences.
Query variants and run Variant Effect Predictor workflows.
Find orthologs and homology relationships across species.
Map coordinates between genome assemblies such as GRCh37 and GRCh38.
Use built-in examples for rate-limited Ensembl REST API calls.
limitations: Requires network access to Ensembl or related public documentation hosts.
Depends on Ensembl REST API availability and rate limits.
Does not validate clinical significance or replace expert genomic review.
Large analyses may require batching and downstream processing outside the skill.

use_cases.title: Annotate a Gene List
use_cases.description: Resolve gene symbols to Ensembl IDs, coordinates, transcripts, and external database references.

use_cases.title: Investigate Variant Consequences
use_cases.description: Query variants by rsID or HGVS notation and summarize predicted effects from Ensembl VEP.

use_cases.title: Compare Genes Across Species
use_cases.description: Find orthologs, retrieve sequences, and prepare comparative genomics summaries for model organisms.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up a Gene
prompt_templates.prompt: Look up TP53 in human using Ensembl. Return the Ensembl ID, genomic location, description, and main transcript information.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve a Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Retrieve the genomic sequence for human BRCA2 using its Ensembl gene ID. Explain the sequence type and assembly used.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Variant
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Ensembl VEP to analyze rs699 in human. Summarize predicted consequences, affected genes, and population frequency fields if available.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Comparative Genomics Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Find mouse orthologs for human BRCA2, retrieve their Ensembl IDs, compare available sequence information, and outline next analysis steps.

output: Returns the Ensembl gene identifier and genomic coordinates.
Summarizes the gene description and available transcript information.
Identifies the species and assembly context used for the query.

output_examples.input: Analyze variant rs699 with Ensembl VEP.
output: Lists predicted variant consequences and affected genomic features.
Includes population frequency fields when Ensembl returns them.
Notes that clinical interpretation requires expert review.

output_examples.input: Find orthologs for human TP53 in mouse.
output: Queries Ensembl homology data for the source gene.
Reports matching ortholog identifiers and species names.
Suggests follow-up sequence or conservation analysis.

best_practices: Specify species, genome assembly, and identifier type in every request.
Use batch endpoints and caching for large gene or variant lists.
Record the Ensembl release or assembly when results support publications.
anti_patterns: Treating VEP predictions as final clinical interpretations.
Mixing GRCh37 and current assembly coordinates without mapping.
Sending many single-item requests without rate limit handling.

faq.question: What is Ensembl?
faq.answer: Ensembl is a public genome database from EMBL-EBI that provides annotations, sequences, variants, and comparative genomics data.

faq.question: Does this skill need internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. It queries the public Ensembl REST API and related documentation resources.

faq.question: Can it analyze variants?
faq.answer: Yes. It can query variants and use Ensembl VEP endpoints to summarize predicted consequences.

faq.question: Can it work with older genome assemblies?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents GRCh37 access and coordinate mapping between assemblies.

faq.question: Is it limited to human data?
faq.answer: No. Ensembl supports many species, and the skill includes workflows for cross-species orthology.

faq.question: Does it replace bioinformatics review?
faq.answer: No. It retrieves and organizes Ensembl data, but expert review is needed for scientific or clinical conclusions.
